coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 8
record.summary: Mid-rise market-rate residential block between Maryland and Delaware streets, south of Humboldt St and north of Power Station Park East, approved March 2, 2022 for a Foster + Partners-designed 14-story, approximately 125-ft, 339-unit building with about 18,000 sq ft of retail; in August 2026 JPMorgan Chase agreed to finance roughly $200 million for a 342-unit building at 151 Humboldt St, with construction expected to begin in fall 2026.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land within the former power station site (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram via multi-point real-street georeferencing (see digitization_method), but this diagram is dated Feb 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the adjacent UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 via GDAL GCP/TPS georeferencing -- see digitization_method. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third pass) in a single consistent pixel-detection pass across the whole block layout -- see digitization_method. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth pass) after fixing a mis-measured GCP -- see digitization_method.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Figure 6.2.3 shows Block 8 with a split height: 90 ft (base, small corner) / 125 ft / 85 ft across its width -- the D4D's Permitted Uses table confirms residential is permitted here. Foster + Partners-designed residential building per press coverage, warm metallic patina and rhythmic facade modulation facing Power Station Park per some sources; unit count reported inconsistently across sources (249 vs. 339 vs. a separately-cited 355 units in one SF OEWD pipeline-forecast document, est. start Mar 2027-end May 2029, ~$275M) and height reported inconsistently too (140 ft vs. 156 ft in different press articles) -- confirmed as of a Feb 2026 source that construction had not started.

images.license_note: Under SB 1214, SF Planning only posts an applicant's full architectural drawings online if the applicant didn't instead submit a reduced massing-diagram-only set for public distribution; when the full drawings are posted, as here in the published Design Review Approval packet, the applicant's permission for public posting is deemed granted and the Department 'shall not be subject to any restrictions on the copying or distribution' of them. Read 2026-09-18.
images.appeal_note: Full-bleed, sunlit ground-level view from Power Station Park showing greenery, retail canopies and active street life -- one of the strongest renderings in the set.

open_questions: Address / parcel: the Chronicle gives Block 8 as 151 Humboldt St. status.csv's Block 2 row records that blklot 4232022 (151 Humboldt St) sits roughly where the D4D places Block 8. Block 8 may therefore already have a subdivided Assessor parcel (4232022) that could replace this approximate polygon. Not verified against DataSF here; flagged for the geometry owner.

Unit count for the 2026 building (342) differs from the 2022 approval (339) and the compliance reports (348). Whether a revised design review or new site permit has been filed since May 2022 is not documented in the corpus.

Architect: Stanley Saitowitz | Natoma Architects publishes a 'Potrero Power Block 8' concept ('initial thoughts to begin the process of developing a design for Block 8', architect's own material, undated). The Chronicle (Aug 2026) still credits Foster + Partners and uses its renderings. Not recorded as a fact; noted here only.

Height: the approved plan set shows 125 ft to the last occupied floor with mechanical screening to 145 ft; SF YIMBY reported 140 ft (2021) and 156 ft (2022). The geometry file's note ('140 ft vs. 156 ft') reflects the press figures, not the approval.

No construction start found. Searched the 2021-2024 compliance reports, SF YIMBY (Block 8 category, last item March 2022), the Chronicle and SF Standard. The Aug 2026 Chronicle says construction 'is expected to begin in the fall' of 2026; no groundbreaking report yet as of Sept 17, 2026.
The geometry file's regulatory_context cites an OEWD pipeline document with 355 units, an estimated start of March 2027 and about $275M; that document is not in the corpus and could not be verified.
No general contractor, total development cost, or ground-lease information for Block 8 in any source found (developer-owned land; no Port lease).

The 2028 completion figure used for the new expected-completion milestone comes from SF YIMBY's March 2021 report of Planning filings; no source since has restated a completion year for the 342-unit building financed in August 2026, so this is treated as a record-specific but stale estimate rather than a current commitment.
